flexion-extension.def: Flexion is a sagittal-plane movement that decreases the angle between two bones or bends the trunk or neck forward; extension increases the angle and returns the part toward anatomical position. Hyperextension is extension past anatomical position, and hyperflexion is flexion beyond the normal range.

abduction-adduction.def: Abduction moves a limb away from the midline of the body in the frontal plane; adduction moves it back toward the midline. Fingers abduct away from the middle finger and toes away from the second toe.

rotation-circumduction.def: Rotation turns a bone around its own long axis; in a limb it is medial rotation if the front of the limb turns toward the midline and lateral rotation if it turns away. Circumduction moves the end of a limb in a circle, sweeping a cone, by flexion, abduction, extension and adduction in sequence. The scapula's superior and inferior rotation tip its glenoid cavity up and down.

special-movements.def: Movements found at only a few joints: supination (palm forward or up) and pronation (palm backward or down, radius crossing the ulna) of the forearm; dorsiflexion and plantar flexion at the ankle; inversion and eversion of the sole; protraction and retraction; elevation and depression; lateral and medial excursion of the jaw; lateral flexion of the trunk or neck; and opposition and reposition of the thumb.
